results.note: Free-text variant (raise site #12), not the fixed "INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION" string used by INV-008/INV-020 (raise sites #18/#6). Target is ENROLLED because the precondition sets eligibility_result=eligible=true, which drives evaluate_and_transition_screening to attempt subject_obj.status = "ENROLLED"; RANDOMIZED's allowed-transition set does not include ENROLLED, so the ORM @validates guard rejects it.

results.note: Demonstrates the genuine bare catch-all at subjects.py:643-644 (raise site #19). The harness should assert status=400 and that the body's detail equals whatever message the injected fault carried, not a fixed string — that's the point of this gap (arbitrary internal failures leak their message verbatim as a 400).

Spurious lock: the subject's demographics were never actually mutated, but the corrupted existing ciphertext silently decrypts to current_demo={} (raise site #22's suppressed exception), which then compares unequal to any non-empty submitted payload. A .NET port that fails loudly on the existing-ciphertext decrypt instead would produce a different status here (see 01_spec.md §5.1 #22's recommendation) — this fixture captures today's actual (arguably wrong) legacy behavior for parity baselining, not the recommended fix.
Same fixed-string body as INV-008 — a malformed state name ("ENROLED") and a legal-but-forbidden transition are indistinguishable in the response, per 01_spec.md §5.1 #6.

exception.message: Transition from None to ENROLLED is forbidden.

results.note: Not a legacy behaviour: the legacy system stored the time of the request as the signed date. The .NET port rejects the request (#4824). The code is carried in the ProblemDetails `code` extension, like INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION.
